title: staged-prompt-prewarm-state-machine-draft
body:
Context and motivation:

We see tail-latency spikes for cold client sessions when a user triggers a long-context generation (e.g., >1k tokens). For interactive products this shows up as a multi-second first-response stall even when the model can handle later tokens fast due to warmed KV/cache. We need a lightweight, low-risk approach to prewarm causal state (KV, prefix activations, tokenizer hints) across the common prompts patterns without overloading GPUs or breaking privacy boundaries.

Goal:
- Define a per-session staged prewarm state machine that supports incremental prefetching of: tokenizer maps, prefix KV segments, and small partial generation traces (shadow prefixes) before the first live request or while a request is streaming.
- Keep memory and compute bounded (budgeted prefetch), allow graceful cancellation, and expose observability hooks for experiment metrics.
- Provide a minimal API shape that client SDKs can opt into.

Assumptions:
- Clients can send a short "expected intent" hint (opaque tag) but not necessarily full user data.
- Server-side model variants support partial KV materialization by token-range (or by chunked key ranges).
- Privacy: we never prewarm using customer PII; prewarm is driven only by client-provided hints and previously observed anonymized prompt clusters.

Design summary (high-level):
- Session lifecycle extension: each Session has a PrewarmState machine with stages: Idle -> HintReceived -> TokenizerWarm -> KVChunkWarm (0..N) -> ShadowGenerate -> Ready -> Expired.
- Budgeting: configurable tokens/KB/compute-per-session; global admission control to avoid concurrent storms.
- API: clients optionally call /sessions/{id}:prewarm with an intent hint and prewarm level preferences; server returns a prewarm ticket and expected timeline and can stream progress updates.
- Heuristics: prewarm more aggressively for recently-active sessions, paid tiers, and intents mapped to high-latency prompts.

API shape (proposal):
- Request: POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/prewarm
  - body fields (client):
    - intent_hint: string (freeform tag, small)
    - prewarm_profile: ["minimal"|"balanced"|"aggressive"]
    - max_budget_ms: int (client preference; server may cap)
    - allow_shadow_generate: bool (client opt-in to letting server do short synthetic generation to warm KV)
  - response: 202 Accepted + JSON { ticket_id, estimated_completion_ms, stages: [list] }
- Progress stream: GET /v1/prewarm/{ticket_id}/events (server-sent events or websocket)
  - events: stage_started, stage_completed, stage_skipped, error, metrics-snippet

PrewarmState machine (detailed):
- Idle: no prewarm work.
- HintReceived: client provided intent_hint; admission control called. If rejected -> Idle with reason.
- TokenizerWarm: ensure tokenizer caches for the request tokenization path (freq maps, bpe cache). Fast and cheap. Usually completes in <10ms.
- KVChunkWarm[i]: materialize KV for token ranges that appear commonly with the intent. We partition KV by logical chunk id (not raw token index) to allow partial loads. Each chunk has cost estimate. We step through 0..N until budget exhausted.
- ShadowGenerate: optional. Run a short deterministic forward pass (e.g., 8 tokens) with low-priority compute to populate transient activations / KV access patterns. Must be strictly bounded by budget and traced for telemetry.
- Ready: session marked prewarmed; subsequent live request can short-circuit cold paths.
- Expired: TTL or explicit cancel; free resources.

State transition table (ascii):

  Idle --(prewarm requested)--> HintReceived
  HintReceived --(admitted)--> TokenizerWarm
  HintReceived --(rejected)--> Idle
  TokenizerWarm --(done)--> KVChunkWarm[0]
  KVChunkWarm[i] --(budget remains)--> KVChunkWarm[i+1]
  KVChunkWarm[i] --(budget exhausted)--> ShadowGenerate? or Ready
  KVChunkWarm[N] --(done)--> ShadowGenerate?
  ShadowGenerate --(done)--> Ready
  Ready --(ttl||session-end||cancel)--> Expired

Notes on chunking approach:
- Chunk keys are derived from model attention-kernel friendly boundaries (e.g., 64-token windows, sentence-level boundaries for long documents).
- We store chunk metadata: chunk_id, estimated_size_bytes, estimated_compute_ms, last_used_bucket. These live in metadata service (not in this doc's schema).
- Admission control uses a simple token-bucket style pool and per-node concurrency cap.

Telemetry and SLOs to capture:
- prewarm.request.count (by profile, intent_tag)
- prewarm.admit.rate, prewarm.reject.reason
- prewarm.stage.latency.{tokenizer,kv-chunk,shadow}
- prewarm.resource.ms (compute), bytes_loaded
- prewarm.effectiveness: first-request delta in latency (p50/p95) for prewarmed vs baseline
- safety: count of canceled/expired prewarms that had non-empty shadow generate

Implementation sketch (server pseudocode):

  onPrewarmRequest(session_id, body):
    ticket = allocateTicket(session_id, body.prewarm_profile)
    if not admit(ticket):
      return 202 { ticket, admitted:false, reason }
    enqueueWork(ticket)
    return 202 { ticket, admitted:true }

  workerLoop(ticket):
    setState(ticket, 'TokenizerWarm')
    warmTokenizer(ticket.session, ticket.intent)
    for chunk in selectChunks(ticket.intent, budget):
      setState(ticket, 'KVChunkWarm')
      materializeChunk(chunk)
      recordMetrics(chunk)
      if budgetExhausted: break
    if ticket.allow_shadow_generate and budgetRemaining:
      setState(ticket, 'ShadowGenerate')
      runLowPriorityForwardPass(ticket.session, seed_prompt)
    setState(ticket, 'Ready')

Client SDK considerations:
- Keep API surface small. Default to prewarm_profile=balanced and allow opt-out.
- Expose a small async callback or Promise that resolves when prewarm is Ready or returns a progress handle for UX (spinner -> instant response).
- Fallback: clients that don’t call prewarm still get server-side opportunistic warming (see experiments section).

Privacy and security:
- Intent hints must be <= 128 bytes and flagged as non-PII. The server may normalize and classify hints into anonymized buckets.
- Shadow generate must never persist generated tokens beyond ephemeral traces used for warming; audits will assert no customer PII is written to logs.

Experimentation plan:
- A/B: enable prewarm for 5% of sessions in a targeted product (web chat) for 2 weeks. Measure first-response p50/p95 and GPU overhead.
- Profile tiers: run separate experiments for free vs paid tiers to tune admission policy.
- Safety: run comparative QA to ensure shadow-generated prefixes don’t cause model drift for later live generations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to derive chunk boundaries for large attention windows across multiple model families? (RL: need heuristics per-architecture)
- Budget defaults per profile? Start with minimal: 30ms compute, 4 chunks, no shadow by default.
- Admission control knobs surfaced to Console (per-namespace override).

Minimal next steps (developer checklist):
- [ ] Spike: implement tokenizer warm path and measure cost on a node (2d)
- [ ] Spike: KV chunk materialize API prototype + unit test (3d)
- [ ] Build ticketing + worker loop (4d)
- [ ] Small scale experiment (5% traffic) + telemetry dashboards (1w)

Notes to self:
- Keep prewarm stateless where possible; ticket + ephemeral worker makes cancellation simple.
- Don’t over-index on shadow generate early; tends to be harder to bound.
- Talk to product team about an opt-in UX for prewarming on premium tiers.

References and related docs:
- see: https://confluence.redwood/infra/prewarm-ideas (internal)
- related: session-probe-playbook.json, client-edge-fallback-heuristics-brain-dump.json (drive)

End of scratchpad.
